title: Frame the problem, test a claim, revise from results
problem: How can the three complementary tools help choose a useful next action?
outcome: A scoped problem, a checked claim and an informative small test.
note: A synthetic teaching example. The main path is one analytical planning order, not a mandatory sequence stated by the source. Conditions and feedback may change the appropriate next tool.

nodes.title: Frame the problem
nodes.action: Record the boundary, stakeholders, constraints and an observable success criterion.
nodes.check: Check that the criterion is observable and the boundary is explicit.

sources.quote: When the scope is unclear, draw a problem map first

nodes.title: Check the claim
nodes.input: A claim and its supporting observations.
nodes.action: Separate observations from explanations and seek competing explanations and counterevidence.
nodes.output: A traceable claim with its remaining uncertainty.
nodes.check: Do not treat one observation as proof.

nodes.title: Run a small informative test
nodes.input: An important assumption and a prediction.
nodes.action: Run a low-cost test, compare its result with the prediction and revise the assumption before scaling.
nodes.output: New information for the next decision.
nodes.check: Compare result and prediction before scaling.

sources.quote: The result can update the evidence chain

edges.condition: The boundary and criterion are explicit.
edges.why: An analytical planning order: scope can focus evidence gathering; the source does not mandate this sequence.

edges.condition: An important assumption can be tested at low cost.
edges.why: An analytical planning order: the claim identifies what the small test can examine.

edges.condition: Discussion stalls and a small informative test is feasible.
edges.handoff: The scoped problem and an important assumption.
edges.why: The source proposes a small test when discussion stalls; the branch is a conditional analytical placement.

edges.condition: Results differ from the prediction: revise the claim.
edges.handoff: The new observations from the test.
edges.why: The source says the result can update the evidence chain.

edges.condition: Constraints change: revisit the problem boundary.
edges.why: The source says changed constraints can send the reader back to the problem map.
